---
title: Conformance
---

Conformance is demonstrated with test vectors. A verifier that produces the expected status for
every vector, and a signer whose output the reference verifier accepts, conform to SIB/1. The
vectors are generated by the reference implementation and checked against its verifier before
they are written, so they are known-good by construction.


## Requirements by Target

Signer
: Produces blocks that the reference verifier reports as `verified` with the signer's registry
  entry, for instructions under both `text/1` and `raw/1`, including instructions containing
  typographic quotes, non-breaking spaces and multiple lines. Shows the canonical instruction and
  the header terms before signing. Emits a visible dev-mode warning for a software key. For a
  WebAuthn key, sets the challenge to the hash of the signing input and refuses to emit a block
  whose assertion does not verify.

Verifier
: Produces the expected status for every vector below. Applies the steps of
  [Verification](verification.qmd) in order. Carries the block's claims on every failing result.
  Emits the [manifest](manifest.qmd) schema for a document containing several blocks, some
  failing, in discovery order.

Harness
: Runs the verifier before its permission decision on every tool call. Delivers the manifest on
  a channel the agent cannot write to. Fails closed when the verifier or the classifier fails.
  Records the manifest for each decision.


## Vector Format

The vectors live in `docs/spec/vectors/`, one JSON file each, listed in `index.json`. Each file
holds:

```json
{
  "name": "expired",
  "note": "why this vector exists",
  "block": "-----BEGIN SIB SIGNED INSTRUCTION-----\n...",
  "registry": {"signers": [{"signer": "alice@example.com", "keys": [ ... ]}]},
  "inputs": {"now": "2026-09-13T12:00:00Z", "audience": "acme/dev-agent", "mode": "dev"},
  "expected_status": "expired",
  "expected_text": "canonical instruction, or null when the rule is unknown"
}
```

A verifier under test is given `block`, `registry` and `inputs`, with a nonce store that accepts
everything, and MUST produce `expected_status`. `registry` MAY carry a top-level
`allowed_aaguids` object, which extends the built-in biometric-capable allowlist for the vectors
that use it. Where `expected_text` is not null it MUST also
report that canonical text. The generator, `docs/spec/vectors/generate.py`, creates a fresh dev
key and a fresh software WebAuthn authenticator on every run, so signatures differ between runs
and statuses do not.


## Vectors

| Vector | Expected status | What it checks |
|---|---|---|
| `verified` | `verified` | The block as signed. |
| `verified_after_transport` | `verified` | Quoted with `> ` and one line re-wrapped; the canonical text is unchanged. |
| `invalid_signature` | `invalid_signature` | One word of the instruction changed after signing. |
| `metadata_mismatch` | `metadata_mismatch` | A clear metadata line edited; the signed header is intact. |
| `expired` | `expired` | `now` is after `exp`. |
| `not_yet_valid` | `not_yet_valid` | Issued more than 60 seconds after `now`. |
| `audience_mismatch` | `audience_mismatch` | Block audience `acme/ci-agent` presented to `acme/dev-agent`. |
| `unknown_signer` | `unknown_signer` | Signer not in the registry. |
| `unknown_key` | `unknown_key` | Signer is enrolled, this `kid` is not. |
| `unknown_key_wrong_signer` | `unknown_key` | An enrolled `kid` used with a different `iss`. |
| `dev_key_in_enforced_mode` | `dev_key_in_enforced_mode` | The verified block, verifier in enforced mode. |
| `malformed_not_detached` | `malformed` | A payload segment is present; a block must be a detached JWS. |
| `malformed_unknown_canon` | `malformed` | The header names a canonicalization rule the verifier does not know. |
| `revoked` | `revoked` | The key is marked revoked in the registry. |
| `webauthn_verified` | `verified` | Signed by a passkey: UV set, origin and RP ID enrolled, AAGUID allowlisted; verifier in enforced mode. |
| `webauthn_verified_dev_mode` | `verified` | The same block with the verifier in dev mode. |
| `webauthn_invalid_signature` | `invalid_signature` | One word changed after signing; the recomputed challenge no longer matches `clientDataJSON`. |
| `webauthn_uv_not_performed` | `uv_not_performed` | The assertion's UV flag is clear. |
| `webauthn_origin_not_allowed` | `origin_not_allowed` | `clientDataJSON.origin` is not enrolled for the key. |
| `webauthn_rp_id_mismatch` | `rp_id_mismatch` | `rpIdHash` is not the SHA-256 of the enrolled RP ID. |
| `webauthn_unknown_key_wrong_credential` | `unknown_key` | `credentialId` is not the credential enrolled under `kid`. |
| `webauthn_authenticator_not_allowed` | `authenticator_not_allowed` | The registry's allowlist lacks the authenticator's AAGUID. |
| `dev_block_with_passkey_enrolled` | `dev_key_in_enforced_mode` | A dev block with a passkey enrolled and the verifier in enforced mode. |

`nonce_replayed` has no vector in Phase 1, because the reference nonce store accepts every block.
A vector is added with the store in Phase 3.


## Running the Vectors

Against the reference verifier:

```bash
.venv/bin/python docs/spec/vectors/generate.py
```

The script regenerates and checks every vector; a failed assertion names the vector and the
status produced. A third-party verifier reads the JSON files directly.
